summary: Juan Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Cardiff University under the doctoral supervision of Max Deeg (attested 2012).

Judit Törzsök is an Indologist who earned an MA from Eötvös Loránd University and a DPhil from Oxford (Merton College) under Alexis Sanderson. She held posts at the University of Lille (~2000–2017) and EPHE as professor from 2018.

A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Judith Simmer-Brown earned degrees from Cornell College, Florida State, and Walden University. A student of Chögyam Trungpa, she joined Naropa University in 1977, becoming Distinguished Professor Emerita.

Juhn Y. Ahn is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 2007. Ahn serves at the University of Michigan, attested as Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies in 2019.

Juhyung Rhi works in Buddhist studies, art history, and Indology. After earning a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, Rhi became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University in 1992.
Juichiro Tanabe is a scholar in philosophy who studied as a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford (2000–2001) and studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire was a French scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and Bourbon College. He served as Professor of Greek at the Collège de France from 1838 to 1852.

Indologist and linguist Jules Bloch studied at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet. He held posts at INALCO (1921–1937), EPHE (1919–1951), and the Collège de France (1936–1951).

Jules Brooks Levinson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of Virginia in 1994 under Jeffrey Hopkins and was an assistant professor of religion at Hamline University in 1996.

Historian Jules Michelet studied at Lycée Charlemagne. He held positions at the École Normale Supérieure, served as a section head at the Archives nationales (1830–1851), and was Professor of History at the Collège de France (1838–1852).

Historian and linguist Jules Oppert studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, Berlin, and Kiel (PhD ~1847). He served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative philology at INALCO (1857) and as professor at the Collège de France (1874–1905).

Julia A. B. Hegewald is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She earned a BA and PhD from SOAS University of London, an MA from the University of Oxford, and completed her habilitation at RWTH Aachen University (~2003–2008).

Julia Ching was a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned degrees from Catholic University of America and Australian National University. She taught at Columbia and Yale before becoming a professor at the University of Toronto in 1978.

Julia F. Andrews is a scholar of sinology and art history who studied at Brown University, Harvard University, and the University of California, Berkeley. She held a post at Ohio State University beginning around 1987.
Julia Leslie was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who held a post at SOAS University of London from 1989 to 2004.

Julian Schott is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Schott is attested in 2026 as a Research Fellow at the University of Hamburg and a faculty member at the University of Vienna.

Juliane Schober is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989. She held posts as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University (attested 1997, 2007).
Julie Gifford is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds. She held a post at Miami University, attested in 2011.
Julius Dutoit was a scholar in the fields of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Adalbert Kuhn and Ernst Kuhn (~1895–1904).

Indologist Julius Eggeling studied at Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1869–1875) and held the Sanskrit professorship at the University of Edinburgh from 1875 to 1914.
